crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Routing Across Automated Market Makers
children.blurb: Routing across automated market makers is the practice of finding and executing a trade path through one or more on-chain liquidity pools to get a desired asset at a better effective price than a single pool would offer.

children.name: Yield Strategies in Smart Contracts
children.blurb: Yield strategies in smart contracts cover onchain methods for earning a return on crypto assets by placing them into decentralised finance protocols.

children.name: On-Chain Forensics
children.blurb: On-chain forensics is the practice of tracing activity on public blockchains to identify who moved what, when, and why.

children.name: Stablecoin Stress Testing
children.blurb: Stablecoin stress testing covers the set of analyses that ask how a stablecoin's peg, reserves and redemption process behave under adverse conditions.

children.name: Governance Token Outcomes
children.blurb: Governance token outcomes are the results that follow votes, delegation and proposal execution in token based communities.

sections.body: Crypto markets and decentralised finance are a set of protocols and venues where assets trade, collateral moves, and rules are enforced by code. Artificial intelligence is being used here less to predict prices and more to operate inside these systems: choosing routes across automated market makers, allocating capital among smart contract yield sources, clustering wallet behaviour for investigations, simulating stablecoin redemptions under stress, and reading governance proposals and voting patterns. These are engineering and data problems, not just forecasting problems, because every action settles on a public ledger and every failure is visible. The work overlaps with market microstructure, mechanism design, and security, and it often runs against adversarial conditions where other participants adapt to any automated strategy. The site's 222 compliance and regulation pages provide context for the rules that surround these activities, though the pages in this section focus on the technical and economic mechanics.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Some parts are relatively mature. Route optimisation across automated market makers is a well studied problem, with algorithms that split orders, compare pools, and account for fees and slippage, though latency, MEV, and changing liquidity mean no router is permanently optimal. Yield strategies in smart contracts are widely automated, but they are fragile to contract bugs, oracle failures, liquidity crunches, and incentive changes, and backtests often overstate what live execution can capture. On-chain forensics has become a practical discipline, with clustering, graph analysis, and anomaly detection used by exchanges, analysts, and investigators, yet privacy tools, mixers, and cross chain bridges create real gaps. Stablecoin stress testing remains hard because redemption behaviour, reserve quality, and market confidence interact in ways that historical data only partly captures. Governance token outcomes are the least settled area, since voting power, delegation, and token incentives produce results that are difficult to generalise from one protocol to another. The honest limit across all of these pages is that AI can improve measurement, routing, and detection, but it cannot remove counterparty risk, code risk, or the possibility that a market structure changes faster than a model can adapt.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages in this section form a chain from execution to strategy to oversight to systemic risk to governance. Routing Across Automated Market Makers is the entry point for how trades are placed and how AI compares venues, so a reader goes there for the mechanics of order flow and slippage. Yield Strategies in Smart Contracts follows the capital after it is deployed, covering how automated agents choose and rebalance positions and where those strategies break. On-Chain Forensics is the investigative counterpart, showing how AI traces funds, clusters addresses, and supports compliance work after or during suspicious activity. Stablecoin Stress Testing zooms out to the stability of the settlement asset itself, asking how AI models simulate runs, redemptions, and reserve pressure. Governance Token Outcomes closes the section by looking at what happens when token holders vote and delegate, and how AI can read proposals, participation, and power concentration. Together they cover the full loop of trading, earning, investigating, stress testing, and governing in decentralised markets.
